reason: E1 states that high configurational entropy stabilizes the solid-solution phase and that severe lattice distortion causes low atomic diffusivity, supporting the first two premises. E2 provides direct evidence for sluggish diffusion preventing phase separation in multi-element nanoparticles, supporting the third premise. However, neither passage provides evidence for the dominance of sluggish diffusion at temperatures up to 1923 K or for the decoupling of bulk and surface diffusion in nanoparticles, leaving the last two premises unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: High configurational entropy in equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn stabilizes a single solid-solution phase against intermetallics or segregation
Severe lattice distortion in this HEA causes low atomic diffusivity (sluggish diffusion)
Sluggish diffusion kinetically prevents phase separation and elemental segregation
The sluggish diffusion effect is the dominant factor governing structural stability up to 1923 K
Bulk sluggish diffusion can be isolated from surface diffusion effects in nanoparticles
